$comment: Review record for the supplement inputs. One group per (field_path, method) -- one judgment call, however many times it was applied: 'identity.since from general knowledge' is a single decision made 524 times, not 524 decisions. Each group carries every member entry key and one exemplar value with its note and citation. This is the corpus's largest body of unverified content: supplement values are needs_approval by construction yet promote unreviewed by default, and ~97% carry method=general_knowledge, meaning there is no citation to check them against -- only a human who knows the PPM. The `groups` list is regenerated; the `status`/`reason`/`reviewed_at`/`exceptions` fields on each group are HAND-EDITED and are preserved verbatim across regenerations. Set status to 'approved' or 'withheld' after reading a group's exemplar; use `exceptions` (entry_key -> {status, reason}) for members that deviate from their group's decision. A group that disappears moves to orphaned_decisions rather than being dropped. Nothing consumes this yet: the build chain has been ungated since 2026-07-21, so this records a human judgment rather than gating output. See docs/workflow/review-records.md.

exemplar.note: Introduced with CUDA 4.0's device-centric runtime API, replacing cudaThreadSynchronize. cuda_runtime_api.h carries no per-routine version marker.
The calling host thread waits; the work it waits for is the device's, not this call's.
The CUDA runtime API may be called concurrently from multiple host threads; NVIDIA's API synchronization-behavior page notes only that such calls can contend for internal resources.
Touches only the calling process's own host and device memory.
Complete on return: everything issued before it has finished.

[corrected 2026-07-21, second field audit] MPI_Init's argv is `char ***argv` -- the process command line, which the implementation may read and prune before any device is in play. It is not a data buffer participating in a transfer, so the CUDA-aware-MPI 'either' case cannot apply to it: no implementation accepts a device pointer here. The previous value carried the buffer-parameter boilerplate verbatim (and dragged a matching context_dependencies entry and buffer_aliasing value along with it), reached because Extract's parameter_kind names argv a BUFFER for its own array-of-strings reason -- which is about what the parameter structurally is, not about which memory it may live in.

apis.json itself carries length=null for buf (confirmed by direct inspection of external-inputs/mpi/tex/mpi-standard/apis.json) -- it only ever populates this field for genuine array-of-arrays parameters (e.g. Allgatherv's recvcounts/displs), never for the ordinary buffer+count pair, even though the pairing is unambiguous here: buf is immediately followed by count ('number of elements in send buffer') in both the parameter order and the binding block's own desc text. This is the standard MPI buffer+count convention, not a per-function judgment call.

[added 2026-08-09] The data-movement shape: source on the single PE named by PE_root is copied to dest on every PE participating in the collective.
[added 2026-08-09] The routine is defined over an OpenSHMEM team, which is a group of PEs within one program -- the intracommunicator case. OpenSHMEM defines no intercommunicator analogue.
[added 2026-08-09] A broadcast takes no reduction operator; the signature has no operator argument and the description states a copy, not a combination.

[added 2026-08-09] A distinguished root plays an asymmetric role -- PE_root supplies the data all other PEs receive. Note the team-based form updates dest on *all* PEs including the root, where the deprecated active-set form updates it on all PEs other than the root; root_involved is true in both, since it asks about the asymmetric role, not about who is written.

[added 2026-08-09] A blocking collective's contract is that every participant's result is in place by the time the call returns -- distinct from a put, whose remote side is only guaranteed after a quiet. Matches the value on mpi_bcast and nvshmem_{T}_broadcast; the deprecated shmem_broadcast32 carries it too.
